open_points.subject: A14 — binary media-type resolution
open_points.text: the media type is resolved from the leading signature bytes of the stored content against a closed list per object kind (expense document: PDF, JPEG, PNG; progress photo: JPEG, PNG, WebP)
open_points.question: What exact byte signatures, signature lengths, variant rules, and precedence determine each permitted media type, including content matching more than one signature or a truncated signature?
options: Define an ordered exact signature table for every permitted type
Delegate recognition to a named library and fix its version and accepted results
Reject every ambiguous or incomplete signature
open_points.default_guess: Use an ordered exact magic-byte table, require enough bytes for a complete match, and reject no-match or ambiguous content.

open_points.subject: A14 — binary download name
open_points.text: the download name is derived from object kind, id and the resolved extension
open_points.question: What exact filename is produced for each object kind, including prefix, separators, identifier representation, extension spelling, and casing?
options: Use `<object_kind>-<uuid>.<extension>`
Use a fixed per-kind prefix followed by the canonical UUID and lowercase extension
Leave naming to the HTTP adapter
open_points.default_guess: Use a fixed per-kind prefix, a hyphen, the canonical lowercase UUID, and the lowercase resolved extension.

open_points.subject: A25 — request and binary bound ordering
open_points.text: Request bodies and binary responses are bounded by runtime settings before expensive work
open_points.question: Which operations count as expensive work, and at what exact point must each request-body and binary-response bound be checked?
options: Reject the request before routing or handler invocation, and abort binary reading as soon as its bound would be exceeded
Permit authorization and metadata lookup before a bounded binary read
Read the complete binary and reject only before response emission
open_points.default_guess: Reject an oversized request before handler invocation; for binaries, authorize and resolve metadata first, then perform a bounded read that aborts immediately when the limit would be exceeded.

witness.initial: A permitted document references a stored object larger than the configured binary bound.
events: An authenticated client requests the document.
The owner authorizes the object and binary delivery applies the bound.
outcomes: The storage reader stops at the bound and the remainder is never read.
The complete object is read into memory and only then refused before response emission.
witness.observer: The service operator sees different storage I/O, memory use, and latency.

open_points.subject: A25 — log redaction
open_points.text: Logs redact authorization, cookie and secret-like names.
open_points.question: What exact field names, header names, matching normalization, and name-pattern rule define “secret-like names,” and is the value removed, replaced, or partially masked?
options: Use an exact closed case-insensitive name set
Use the closed set plus specified suffix and substring patterns
Redact every structured field not explicitly allow-listed
open_points.default_guess: Use a closed case-insensitive set plus explicit token, secret, password, authorization, and cookie name patterns, replacing the whole value with a fixed marker.

witness.initial: A request causes a structured log field named `client_secret_hint` to be emitted.
events: The transport logger applies its interpretation of “secret-like names”.
outcomes: The field value is fully redacted because its name contains `secret`.
The field value is logged because only exact names are redacted.
witness.observer: Anyone with access to service logs sees the difference.

open_points.subject: A25 — TRN-001
open_points.text:
- TRN-001, TRN-002, TRN-003: the runtime behaviour check
  [witness: verification:runtime_behavior_client_portal].
- TRN-001, TRN-003: the transport guard check
  [witness: verification:transport_guard_client_portal].
open_points.question: What must these checks show for TRN-001, including the untrusted-host cases, the exact oversized-body boundary, and proof that no handler was reached?
options: Require explicit cases for every host refusal and for a body exactly one unit over the bound, with a handler sentinel proving no invocation
Rely only on the named checks without prescribing assertions
open_points.default_guess: Require explicit untrusted-host and oversized-body cases and a handler sentinel that remains untouched.

open_points.subject: A25 — TRN-002
open_points.question: What must the check show separately for foreign-origin viewer sign-out and for a viewer project read without the cookie?
options: Require one refusal case for every origin mismatch dimension and one no-cookie project-read refusal
Require only one representative refusal for each half of the invariant
Rely only on the named check without prescribing assertions
open_points.default_guess: Require explicit foreign-scheme, foreign-host, and foreign-effective-port sign-out refusals plus a project-read refusal with no viewer cookie.

open_points.subject: A25 — TRN-003
open_points.text:
- TRN-001, TRN-003: the transport guard check
  [witness: verification:transport_guard_client_portal].
open_points.question: What credential, cookie, and secret inputs and which log sinks must the check inspect to demonstrate that TRN-003 holds?
options: Exercise every authentication contour and inspect every emitted log record
Exercise representative bearer, cookie, and password cases only
Rely only on the named check without prescribing assertions
open_points.default_guess: Exercise staff passwords, viewer cookies and codes, service bearer credentials, authorization headers, and secret-like structured fields, then inspect every captured log record and rendered exception.

open_points.subject: A30 — REGISTRY_BASE_URL start-up validation
open_points.text:
The start-up check refuses only a missing value or
one that is empty or whitespace only, tested on the value as supplied (the
row's normalization is `none`)
open_points.question: Must a whitespace-only `REGISTRY_BASE_URL` stop start-up, or must it be accepted because it is non-empty and values of every form are accepted at start?
options: Reject missing, empty, and whitespace-only values
Reject only a missing or zero-length value
Accept every present value and defer all validation to the gateway
open_points.default_guess: Reject missing, zero-length, and whitespace-only values at start.

witness.initial: Every required environment variable is valid and `REGISTRY_BASE_URL` is three space characters.
events: The host operator starts the service.
outcomes: The normative configuration rule stops start-up because the value is whitespace only.
The CFG-002 Required tests rule accepts start-up because the value is non-empty whatever its form.
witness.observer: The host operator sees whether the service starts.

open_points.subject: A30 — CFG-002 Required tests
open_points.text:
a
  non-empty one is accepted at start whatever its form
open_points.question: How must this Required tests passage be changed to agree with the rule that whitespace-only values are refused without normalization?
options: Say “a non-empty, not-whitespace-only one is accepted at start whatever its other form”
Remove the whitespace-only refusal from the normative rule
Normalize by trimming and test the normalized value
open_points.default_guess: Say that a value containing at least one non-whitespace character is accepted at start whatever its other form.

open_points.subject: A30 — binary read and response bounds
open_points.text:
a binary within
  the read bound but over `max_binary_response_bytes` is not sent; and the
  start is refused when the read bound exceeds the response bound.
open_points.question: How can the first required case occur in a successfully started process when the second rule requires `BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES` to be no greater than `max_binary_response_bytes`?
options: Remove the unreachable within-read/over-response case
Permit the read bound to exceed the response bound and retain the response check
Test the case only after an explicitly supported runtime change to one of the bounds
open_points.default_guess: Keep the start-up relation `read bound <= response bound` and remove the unreachable within-read/over-response test case.

open_points.subject: A30 — credential entropy
open_points.question: Which issued secrets use this value, what does 32 bytes measure, which randomness source is required, and what Required tests must demonstrate the State 1 issuing obligation for viewer and service credentials?
options: Apply 32 raw CSPRNG bytes to every portal-issued credential and session token
Apply it only to viewer and service credentials
Apply it only to the credential-security backend's one-time secrets
open_points.default_guess: Use 32 raw bytes from a cryptographically secure random source for viewer access credentials and service credentials, and require tests of raw entropy length, non-reuse, and verification-only persistence.

open_points.subject: A30 — per-read binary environment values
open_points.text:
the emitted `binary_storage` reads it at each read through its
  backend IR
open_points.question: What happens if `BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES` is missing, invalid, or changed after successful start-up, and which value governs the start-up relation to `max_binary_response_bytes`?
options: Snapshot and retain the start-up value for all reads
Re-read on every operation and translate missing or invalid values to a specified storage failure
Re-read on every operation and stop or fail the process when the value differs from the validated value
open_points.default_guess: Snapshot the validated start-up value and use that immutable value for every read.

events: The host environment is changed so `BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES=2000`.
A client requests a 1500-byte authorized binary.
outcomes: The storage module uses the validated start-up value and refuses the read at 1000 bytes.
The storage module re-reads the environment, accepts the storage read at 2000 bytes, and reaches the separate response bound.
witness.observer: The client and service operator see different failure timing and storage I/O.

open_points.subject: A31 — security-review invariant
open_points.text:
- `python tools/design_lint.py examples/client-portal --state 2`.
- Witness: the State 2 security-review gate of the authoring sequence runs this lint [witness: workbench:state2_rules_decisions].
open_points.question: What must the Required tests show for the invariant that every category has an explicit APPLICABLE, UNRESOLVED, or NOT_APPLICABLE outcome with the required reference, open question, or project-specific rationale?
options: Require an assertion for every category and for the payload required by its selected outcome
Require only that the lint exits successfully
Require representative categories for each outcome
open_points.default_guess: Require enumeration of every review category and assertions that APPLICABLE resolves to an accepted decision, UNRESOLVED to an open question, and NOT_APPLICABLE to a non-empty project-specific rationale.

open_points.subject: Classification principles — binary storage settings
open_points.text:
the one exception is the two binary storage rows
  (`BINARY_STORAGE_ROOT`, `BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES`), which have no field and
  which the emitted `binary_storage` reads at each read, as the Factory's
  binary storage backend is built (A14, A30).
open_points.rule:
Таблица выше —
исчерпывающий список путей значения, и у каждого из них своя форма: перечисление
называется адресом, константа поставщика — `the imported X constant`,
настройка — полем объекта настроек.
open_points.question: Make both environment-dependent binary storage values fields of the settings model delivered through the settings module, or reclassify any non-environment value into one of the other permitted paths.

open_points.subject: A30 — binary read limit delivery
open_points.text:
the emitted `binary_storage` reads it at each read through its
  backend IR (Factory `a6916180314d`). No model-written module reads it.
open_points.rule:
Таблица выше —
исчерпывающий список путей значения, и у каждого из них своя форма: перечисление
называется адресом, константа поставщика — `the imported X constant`,
настройка — полем объекта настроек.
open_points.question: Replace the backend's direct environment read with a field of the settings object handed to the generated code.

open_points.subject: A30 — configuration value paths
open_points.text: except the two binary storage rows, which the emitted `binary_storage` reads.
open_points.rule:
Таблица выше —
исчерпывающий список путей значения, и у каждого из них своя форма: перечисление
называется адресом, константа поставщика — `the imported X constant`,
настройка — полем объекта настроек.
open_points.question: Remove the exception and state the settings-object fields through which the emitted binary storage receives both deployment values.
